reading.body:
CyrusOne's Cincinnati CIN2 publishes 11 MW of IT capacity, which is 18 percent of all disclosed data center load in Ohio, a state where only eight of 77 mapped facilities publish power figures at all.

The disclosure gap is the real finding. Ohio has 77 mapped data center facilities and only eight report power, totaling 60.4 MW between them. CIN2 ranking third among those eight says more about how few facilities disclose than about how large CIN2 is. Any state total built from these numbers understates Ohio's actual load by an unknown amount.

At 11 MW and 143,778 square feet of technical space, CIN2 is sized for regional and regulated workloads. Its certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, and SSAE 16 Type II, point to financial, healthcare, and federal tenants. The reading's conversions, roughly 275 racks at 40 kW per rack or about 34 clusters at 320 kW, are arithmetic applied to the published capacity, not a record of installed hardware.

What the data does not cover matters for AI scaling. There is no grid interconnection figure, no power source, and no announced expansion, which the suitability score lists as missing. Nothing here shows whether CIN2 is limited by available power or by demand for it. The reading puts frontier training at 100+ MW campuses elsewhere, and by that measure an 11 MW facility is not built for that workload.
